ideas.pitch: A defense-in-depth security harness that detects and blocks prompt injection and tool-calling escapes in LLM-powered applications, designed specifically for capture-the-flag style automated vulnerability testing.
ideas.title: PromptShield CTF Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the defense-in-depth and prompt-hardening architecture seen in winning entries like bitgn-pac-agent-public, perfectly aligning with a cybersecurity CTF audience.

ideas.pitch: A localized, jam-resilient network packet inspector and intrusion detection node built for edge deployment during capture-the-flag network challenges.
ideas.title: Aegis-CTF Edge
ideas.why_it_could_win: Adapts the deterministic engagement and edge-defense architecture from Aegis-Edge, appealing directly to technical cybersecurity judges looking for robust network tools.

ideas.pitch: A fine-tuned BERT-powered classifier that scans incoming CTF submission payloads and OSINT communications in real time for obfuscated phishing links and social engineering vectors.
ideas.title: PhishSleuth BERT
ideas.why_it_could_win: Replicates the proven runner-up formula from Cyber-Hackathon-2025 by pairing BERT with a lightning-fast FastAPI backend for immediate threat detection.

ideas.pitch: A zero-knowledge proof authentication gate using Noir circuits that allows players to prove capability or flag ownership on a shared leaderboard without revealing the underlying exploit payload.
ideas.title: ZeroKnow Auth CTF
ideas.why_it_could_win: Employs advanced cryptographic engineering similar to openstoa, satisfying judges who reward technically demanding ZK implementations.

ideas.pitch: An offline acoustic mesh communication protocol for relaying flag fragments across isolated environments where traditional Wi-Fi or internet access is blocked during a physical CTF.
ideas.title: EchoMesh Radio CTF
ideas.why_it_could_win: Brings the unusual physical hardware and offline networking focus of EchoMesh, guaranteeing a standout entry in a room dominated by web apps.
